plan: Economic theory suggests bidding exactly one's private value is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction. With my value at $9, I have no strategic advantage in bidding above or below this amount. Bidding my true value ensures I win if the item is worth more to me than others, and prevents overpaying. Since values are randomly drawn independently each round, past rounds are irrelevant. I will bid my exact private value.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly my private value ($20) is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed bid auction. This strategy ensures I maximize expected profit by:
1. Winning when my value exceeds others
2. Never overpaying beyond my true valuation
3. Avoiding the risk of underbidding and losing a potentially profitable item
With no previous round history and a single-round game, following the theoretical optimal strategy seems most rational.

This strategy (called "truthful bidding") minimizes the risk of overbidding and losing money, while ensuring I maximize potential profit if I win.
